questions.question: Sales are R3 600 000 and cost of sales R2 400 000. Gross profit, and the mark-up on cost, are:
Net profit before tax is R600 000. Income tax at the company rate of 27 percent is:
options: R162 000, leaving net profit after tax of R438 000
R168 000, leaving net profit after tax of R432 000
R216 000, leaving net profit after tax of R384 000

questions.question: Interest expense is R50 000 on a loan of R500 000. The interest rate the examiner may ask for is:
The correct order of the income statement chain is:
options: Operating profit, gross profit, net profit before tax, tax
Gross profit, net profit after tax, operating profit, tax
Sales, tax, gross profit, operating profit
Gross profit, operating profit, net profit before tax, net profit after tax

subtopics.title: Share Capital, Buy-backs and Retained Income

questions.question: Share capital of R1 950 000 over six hundred thousand shares gives an average issue price of:
options: R3,25 — the key figure for any buy-back working
R3,90 — the mid-point of the two prices

questions.question: Forty thousand shares are repurchased at R4,00 when the average issue price is R3,25. Retained income decreases by:
options: R30 000 — forty thousand times the 75 cents above the average
Nothing — only share capital is affected

questions.question: In the same buy-back, the credit to bank is:
options: R160 000 — the full repurchase price, equal to the two debits combined

questions.question: Opening retained income R288 000, net profit after tax R438 000, dividends R324 000. The closing balance is:
options: R402 000 — and the unpaid final dividend of R180 000 also appears as a current liability

subtopics.title: Cash Flow Signposts and the Three Workings

questions.question: Tax charge R162 000; SARS owed R15 000 at the start and R21 000 at the end. Tax PAID is:
options: R156 000 — charge plus opening owed minus closing owed
R162 000 — always equal to the charge

questions.question: Last year's final dividend was R150 000, this year's interim R144 000, this year's final R180 000. Dividends PAID this year:
options: R294 000 — last year's final plus this year's interim; this year's final is still a liability

questions.question: In a Grade 12 cash flow statement, the disposal of fixed assets is recorded at:
options: Carrying value — by policy, no profit or loss on disposal is introduced

questions.question: Proceeds of a new share issue appear in the cash flow statement under:
options: They do not appear, as shares are not cash
Financing activities — together with buy-backs and loan movements

subtopics.title: The Indicators That Decide the Marks

questions.question: Current assets R690 000, inventories R300 000, current liabilities R300 000. The current and acid-test ratios are:
Return on total capital employed is 25,3 percent while the loan costs 10 percent. The gearing conclusion is:
options: The loan must be repaid at once
Positive gearing — each borrowed rand earns more than it costs, so borrowing for expansion is defensible
The comparison is irrelevant to gearing

questions.question: Net asset value is 392 cents and the shares trade at 460 cents. The 68 cents premium means:
options: The books have understated the assets by error
The market is pricing future prospects the balance sheet cannot record
The share price must fall to 392 cents

questions.question: Earnings per share 73 cents, dividends per share 54 cents. The pay-out policy is roughly:
options: 74 percent paid out — generous to income-seekers, with about a quarter retained for growth

subtopics.title: The Bakery's Year on One Page

questions.question: The bakery's loaves cost R2 400 000 to make and sold for R3 600 000. The baking itself earned:
options: R1 200 000 — every rand of cost became a rand and a half of price

questions.question: The tax collector's slice of company profit is:
options: Fifteen cents in every rand, like VAT
A fixed twenty-seven cents in every rand of profit

questions.question: Each slice earned 73 cents but was paid 54 cents. The 19 cents difference:
options: Stayed in the bakery as retained profit, making every slice worth more
Must be paid out next year by law

questions.question: Profit earned, profit paid and profit kept describe:
options: Sales, cost of sales and gross profit
The three sections of the cash flow statement
Earnings per share, dividends per share and retained income per share

subtopics.title: Following the Cash, Not the Profit

questions.question: The bank balance did not grow by the full profit because:
options: Profit and cash run on different clocks — some charges are unpaid and some payments settle old debts
Cash always equals profit eventually in the same year

questions.question: Of this year's R162 000 tax slice, R21 000 will only be paid next year, and R15 000 of old tax debt was settled. Cash out for tax:
The delivery van wearing out costs profit every year but takes no cash because:
options: The mechanic is paid in cash
Depreciation is a non-cash expense — the cash left when the van was bought
The van belongs to the bank

questions.question: Selling one hundred thousand new slices to cousins for R450 000 brought cash in:
options: As a loan from the cousins
Without a single loaf being baked — a financing inflow, not profit

subtopics.title: Three Questions Before You Buy a Slice

questions.question: The books value a slice at 392 cents but cousins pay 460 cents. The 68 cents extra buys:
options: The bakery's future — customers, location and next year's loaves, which the books may not record

questions.question: The bakery earned 21,2 cents per rand of family money while the bank pays about 8. The extra 13 cents is:
options: The reward for the risk the family carries by investing in a business

questions.question: The whole pot earns 25,3 cents per rand and the loan costs 10. If earning power slid below 10:
options: The loan would start working against the family, because the bank collects in bad years too
The bank would convert the loan to shares

questions.question: The three-sentence habit the examination pays for on every indicator is:
options: Quote the figure, compare it to something, judge with a reason
